hooks.text: A human spacecraft intentionally slammed into a distant asteroid.
We shortened an asteroid's orbit by thirty-two minutes.
An asteroid impact on purpose actually altered a space rock's path.

title: When we crashed a spacecraft into an asteroid
description: We deliberately crashed the DART spacecraft into an asteroid moonlet and shortened its orbit by over half an hour.

beats.text: A human spacecraft intentionally slammed into a distant asteroid.
beats.visual: Artist concept of the DART spacecraft colliding with Dimorphos, NASA, 2022

beats.text: Launched in November 2021, the Double Asteroid Redirection Test mission targeted a small binary system.
beats.visual: SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket launch carrying DART from Vandenberg Space Force Base, 2021

beats.text: Its target was Dimorphos, a tiny moonlet measuring roughly one hundred sixty to one hundred seventy meters wide.
beats.visual: Didymos and Dimorphos system diagram, NASA, 2022

beats.text: Neither Didymos nor Dimorphos posed any actual impact threat to Earth.
beats.visual: Hubble Space Telescope view of the DART impact ejecta, 2022

beats.text: Traveling at approximately fourteen thousand miles per hour, the probe relied entirely on autonomous navigation.
beats.visual: DRACO camera terminal approach image of Dimorphos, NASA, 2022

beats.text: On September 26, 2022, it struck the moonlet while flying about six point eight million miles from Earth.
beats.visual: LICIACube ejecta plume image, Italian Space Agency, 2022

beats.text: The massive kinetic collision shortened [Dimorphos's](/dˈImˈɔɹfˈɑsᵻz/) orbit around [Didymos](/dˈɪdˈImˈɔs/) by thirty-two minutes.
beats.visual: James Webb Space Telescope view of the DART impact, NASA, 2022
queries: James Webb Space Telescope DART impact

beats.text: That astonishing success proved a human spacecraft could intentionally slam into a distant asteroid.
beats.visual: ESA Hera spacecraft asteroid Dimorphos illustration, 2024

better_than_last: Episode ep077 applies a strict scale_ladder structure moving from the mission launch down to the exact asteroid size and final impact speed, ending with a clean loop back to the hook.
